expectations.text: Enhanced system prompt instructs grounding progress claims in actual tool results / evidence (no fabricated status reports)
expectations.evidence: Reporting section of the enhanced prompt: 'Every claim in your progress notes and final report must trace to a command you actually ran in this session — cite test output, not intention. If something is unverified, say so explicitly.'

expectations.text: Enhanced system prompt includes a concrete verification method (e.g., run the migrated tests, verify at intervals) replacing the vague 'double check your work'
expectations.evidence: Concrete method: record a full Jest baseline before changes, then 'migrate a file or coherent group, run those tests under Vitest, confirm parity, then move on', with final full-suite parity against the baseline as the definition of done.

expectations.text: Enhanced system prompt addresses autonomous operation: proceed without asking, don't end turn on a promise or unfulfilled intent
expectations.evidence: 'You run overnight and unattended: no human can answer questions mid-run, so a question ends the work. For any reversible decision that follows from this goal, use your judgment and proceed.' Plus: 'Before ending your turn, check your last paragraph: if it is a plan or a promise ("I'll now run…"), do that work instead of ending.'

expectations.text: Enhanced system prompt defines when stopping/flagging IS appropriate (blocked, irreversible action) rather than pure barrel-through
expectations.evidence: Blocker section: skip-and-log per file, but 'Halt entirely only if continuing would be destructive or the whole approach is invalid (e.g., Vitest cannot be installed) — and if you halt, write the state and reason to MIGRATION_NOTES.md first.'

expectations.text: The vacuous 'You MUST NOT make mistakes' instruction is removed or replaced with actionable behavior
expectations.evidence: The phrase does not appear in the enhanced prompt. Change note: 'Replaced "MUST NOT make mistakes" with a checkable definition of done — an unattended agent can't be errorless by decree; recording a Jest baseline first and targeting parity gives it something it can actually verify.'

expectations.text: Response includes change notes explaining the reasoning behind changes
expectations.evidence: '## What changed and why' with eight bullets, each pairing a change with its rationale (blocker policy, incremental commits, evidence-grounded reporting, anti-early-stopping, scoping, removal of ALL-CAPS exhortations).

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt does not name any specific AI model or vendor
expectations.evidence: The fenced enhanced system prompt contains no AI model or vendor names; only Jest/Vitest (the migration subjects) and generic terms like 'agent' and 'harness'.

claims.claim: Pre-existing test failures are excluded from the agent's responsibility via a recorded baseline
claims.evidence: 'Pre-existing failures are not yours to fix — your target is parity with this baseline, not a green board.' This is a substantive improvement not required by any assertion.

claims.claim: Assumptions were stated in lieu of clarifying questions
claims.evidence: Explicit 'Assumptions made' paragraph: standard Node repo, git available, pre-existing failures preserved, shell access, skip-and-log blocker policy; flags the two assumptions most likely to need tuning.

suggestions.reason: All assertions passed for both old and new skill versions. The versions differ on baseline-parity framing (new) vs 'all passing by morning' (old) — the new framing avoids setting an unachievable goal when pre-existing failures exist. An assertion like 'success criteria account for pre-existing test failures / define a verifiable baseline' would discriminate.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are meaningful but saturated at this skill quality level; consider raising the bar toward baseline handling and resumability.
